test_title: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 24 Jul 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
**Direction: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. Another boy tried his luck and won a comb, a fountain pen, wristwatch and a table lamp one after the other in many chances that he played.

B. An old man won a beautiful clock. The old man did not want the clock, so the shopkeeper took it back and paid 15 rupees to the old man.

C. Bhaiya encouraged him, but Rasheed was not lucky when he tried his luck. He won only cheap items like pencils and an inkbottle, and soon lost all his money.

D. He sold all the items to the shopkeeper and went away happily. Rasheed also wanted to play and try his luck.
solution:
The correct answer is "BADC."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Sentence** B** provides an introduction to the context where individuals are winning prizes, exemplified by an old man's win.
 
• Sentence** A** continues this theme, describing another boy who successfully won multiple items.
 
• Sentence **D** then introduces Rasheed, who, motivated by the successful players, also wants to participate.
 
• Sentence** C **narrates the experience of Rasheed, who unfortunately, doesn't seem to enjoy the same luck as the old man or the other boy, thus providing a conclusive end to the story.

Therefore, the **correct order** of sentences forming a meaningful and coherent paragraph is **'BADC'.**

**Correct sequence**:

 
• **B. **An old man won a beautiful clock. The old man did not want the clock, so the shopkeeper took it back and paid 15 rupees to the old man.
 
• **A. **Another boy tried his luck and won a comb, a fountain pen, wristwatch and a table lamp one after the other in many chances that he played.
 
• **D. **He sold all the items to the shopkeeper and went away happily. Rasheed also wanted to play and try his luck.
 
• **C.** Bhaiya encouraged him, but Rasheed was not lucky when he tried his luck. He won only cheap items like pencils and an inkbottle, and soon lost all his money.
